newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Japanese man missing in northern Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Japanese man missing in northern Cambodia.

text.p: A Japanese man has gone missing in northern Cambodia after crossing over lines between warring Cambodian factions, a Japanese embassy official said on Monday.

The man, a freelance photographer, was with Cambodian government troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen near the northern town of Samrong at the weekend when he crossed over to forces backing ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, the official said.
The man was identified as Kako Kenichi, 29, the official said. His home town was not immediately known.
The Japanese man was a traveller who had been staying in a guest house in the tourist town of Siem Reap for some time but details were sketchy, embassy officials said.

Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh after two days of battles in Phnom Penh on July 5 and 6. Their forces in northern Cambodia clashed soon after and the Prince's forces were pushed back towards Samrong. Fighting flared in the area of Samrong town at the weekend.
